# Bazel qualification

Bazel is experimental. `build-bsd` keeps `bsd-make` as its production backend;
its separate `bazel-test` action qualifies maintained native targets. There is
no complete world, kernel, package, or image Bazel backend yet. Do not use
imported upstream BUILD files as evidence of BSD build coverage.

**Embedded-policy qualification correction (2026-10-27):** symbol, linkage
and DTrace parity alone do not prove signing-input parity. BSDNotify now embeds
and verifies `.5bsd.policy` against Make. BSDLog, BSDAudit, BSDTime and BSDPower
have also been corrected and their full and installed policy payloads verified.
Other CAPIMAGE_MANIFEST consumers still need this integration as their production
binary targets are migrated. BSDNotify daemon installation now also passes. These checks
verify unsigned inputs; signing and runtime trust qualification remain separate.

## Current coverage audit and next work order (2026-10-27, refreshed)

A fresh configured world traversal and component metadata query covers all
**2,103 directories with no query failures**. Of those directories, **596** have
local BUILD/BUILD.bazel files and **1,507** do not. The earlier survey recorded
509/1,594. This is **not a completion percentage**: parent packages can own child
outputs, upstream BUILD files may not implement BSD behavior, and local files can
contain only exports or omit compilation, tests or installation.

The new survey finds 627 program-metadata and 260 library-metadata directories
without local BUILD files; 502 and 243 respectively also lack an ancestor package.
These include test helpers, aggregate directories and multiple-output components,
so they are not counts of missing binaries/libraries. The prior 264-program,
105-library, four-framework and 24-PAM counts were historical checkpoints; they
are not a fresh reconciled qualified-output count. Current qualification remains
component-specific in the evidence entries below.

with native FIDL generation/compiler work, Capsule/Switchboard candidates and
selected native package families. The old statement that those graphs had not

matching kernel; no generator fixture substitutes for that gate.

## Target architecture and completion contract (2026-10-25)

This section is the governing migration design. Historical successful fixtures
below are mechanism evidence, not substitutes for these completion gates. The
final base build must work after base Makefiles and the Make metadata exporters
are removed. Make remains supported for ports and third-party projects. Until the
full qualification gates pass, Make remains the production base backend.

### Ownership and public interface

- Component BUILD files own sources, public/private headers, dependencies,
  generated outputs, tests and install/package membership. Shared Starlark macros
  express common BSD conventions. They must not recreate Make interpretation or
  a second Python/JSON language for the dependency graph.
- Use rules_cc for ordinary compilation/linking and CcInfo for interoperable
  dependencies. BSD rules are justified by concrete unmet semantics: versioned
  ELF ABI, kernel link layout, DTrace mutation, BSD install flags/hardlinks or
  pkgbase archives. Compare standard APIs before retaining a custom rule.
- Proposed aggregate labels are `//:world`, `//:kernel`, `//:packages` and
  `//:release`; these are design interfaces, not currently implemented targets.
  Explicit target suites define supported product coverage; recursive `//...`
  cannot silently substitute for a product inventory.
- Foundry/build-bsd selects platforms, settings, product targets and declared
  external inputs. It invokes Bazel and reports results. It must not duplicate
  dependency ordering, generate component BUILD files or run per-component Make.
  Temporary `make buildworld`, `buildkernel` and `packages` compatibility entry
  points may delegate to Bazel once qualified; the reverse dependency must end.
- Keep Bazel's output/cache state persistent, separate from per-invocation
  evidence directories. Configure standard /usr/obj storage, source identity and
  concurrency locks. Fresh roots are for cold-build tests, not ordinary rebuilds.
  Format-5 source_graph.py now uses persistent source-keyed Bazel state and
  verified cached SDK copies under /usr/obj, with fresh evidence directories.
  The prepared Make SDK still leaves native bootstrap qualification incomplete.

### Configurations, platforms and toolchains

Use platform constraints for target CPU/OS/ABI and execution environments;
registered toolchains select compatible compilers and generator tools. A board
is a product target selecting kernel, firmware and image composition, plus actual
hardware constraints where needed. Do not turn every board into an unrelated
compiler toolchain. Unsupported combinations must fail clearly.

Use typed build settings and select() for base feature choices. Compiler features
own compiler/linker policy; component copts contain actual local requirements.
Production malloc, debug mode, sanitizers, PIC and architecture variants must be
represented in configured dependencies/action keys. Avoid blanket global flags,
per-host probing and arbitrary transitions. Introduce transitions only where a
real dependency requires a different configuration, with analysis tests proving
which settings change. Do not derive release options from a running host.

Execution tools use execution configuration; produced libraries/objects use the
target configuration. C/C++ tools use registered C++ toolchains. FIDL, DTrace and
other reusable generators should expose toolchain contracts when execution or
target selection varies, rather than proliferating unrelated executable attrs.
A cross compiler may run locally while producing target objects; a target test
requires a compatible execution platform or explicit VM harness, never accidental
host execution. Test-only loader paths must not leak into installed artifacts.

### Build option compatibility and pkgbase-only completion gate

The migration must cover configuration inputs, not just the default binaries.
Inventory the maintained world, kernel and package entry points and record each
input as supported, deliberately replaced, or rejected with a diagnostic. Make
is the migration reference; native Bazel configuration becomes the authority.
Do not execute arbitrary make.conf/src.conf logic inside Bazel or silently drop
settings that have no native mapping.

- Support GENERIC and user-supplied kernel configurations, including configuration
  directories, includes, device/options selection and kernel/module selection.
  Preserve configuration identity in the resulting kernel and package metadata.
  Configuration files and their included inputs must be declared dependencies.
- Map TARGET/TARGET_ARCH and supported CPU/ABI choices to platforms/toolchains;
  map WITH_/WITHOUT_ feature choices, production malloc, debug/optimization and
  supported kernel/module options to typed settings and compiler features.
  Resolve defaults and conflicting choices explicitly. Record effective settings
  in the build plan so world, kernel, hardware compatibility checks and packaging
  agree. Unsupported combinations must fail before compilation.
- Keep orchestration choices such as job count, output roots and incremental
  operation distinct from settings that affect artifact contents. Source/config
  changes must invalidate affected actions; job count must not change package
  identity. Preserve explicit configuration-file and CLI precedence.
- Base packaging is pkgbase only. The native package graph must preserve package
  names, splits, dependencies, ABI/version, kernel metadata, manifests and install
  ownership/modes/links. No alternative base package format or distribution-set
  fallback is part of this migration. Ports retain their existing Make builds.
- Qualify GENERIC and a custom kernel configuration, an alternate supported
  target, representative enabled/disabled features, development and production
  builds, package splits, and rejected/contradictory settings. Compare equivalent
  Make outputs during migration and retain native configuration/dependency tests
  after Make is removed. Qualification must include rebuilding after a config
  change to detect stale cached outputs.

Current status: the Make frontend passes KERNCONF/KERNCONFDIR, TARGET/TARGET_ARCH,
SRCCONF and __MAKE_CONF. This does not establish native Bazel support. The current
bazel-test action is a bounded qualification interface and rejects selected
world/profile inputs; full world/kernel/pkgbase configuration remains a required
migration gate. Update the maintained frontend, backend, manual and focused tests
together when this mapping is implemented.

### Bootstrap without cycles

1. Define a versioned bootstrap kit containing Bazel/JDK and compiler/execution
   runtimes, with provenance, licenses, digests, target support and offline inputs.
   It must be obtainable without first building /usr/src with Make.
2. Build host generators and toolchain tools from maintained Bazel targets using
   that kit. Distinguish the compiler's own runtime from target system libraries.
3. Build target headers, startup objects, compiler runtime, libc/libsys and C++
   runtimes with explicit dependencies. Keep the header/bootstrap sysroot separate
   from the completed target SDK to avoid a libc -> whole sysroot -> libc cycle.
4. Build world/kernel and the next compiler/toolkit. Qualify rebuilding from that
   toolkit in a clean environment; compare artifacts with a documented treatment
   of deliberate version/build identity fields.

Current SDK preparation copies a Make-built world and host-loaded runtime files.
A hash of those inputs establishes identity, not bootstrap independence or
hermeticity. Native Bazel bootstrap output-query evidence does not qualify the
JDK/toolchain packaging closure. These remain explicit outstanding gates.

### Generators and kernel graph

FIDL IR/bindings, DTrace provider headers and rewritten objects, RPC, lex/yacc,
NLS, syscall stubs, symbol versions and generated scripts must be separate declared
actions. Pass tools with their runfiles, use Args for scalable command lines,
export providers for generated sources/headers, and declare every consumer edge.
DTrace must receive private output copies when rewriting objects; input mutation
is never acceptable. No generator may discover extra compilation units during
execution and expect Bazel to schedule them afterward.

The kernel needs maintained Bazel configuration/source selections visible during
analysis. Migrate sys/conf/files conditions and device/options ownership into
reviewed BUILD/Starlark definitions and typed configuration. A configuration tool
may emit declared headers and other known outputs; it must not generate a Makefile
that remains the kernel's build graph. Preserve the semantic meaning of supported
kernel configuration inputs, diagnosing unsupported entries. Decide and qualify
the user-facing KERNCONF compatibility adapter before claiming replacement.
Kernel/module rules must cover assembly, linker scripts, offsets, version data,
firmware, module dependencies and target ABI. Native `config` currently calls
makefile() as well as headers(); simply invoking it is not this migration.

### Installation, packages and release

Installation is an artifact graph: source payload plus destination, ownership,
mode, BSD flags, hardlink/symlink identity and package category. Unprivileged
staging must not depend on host user/group resolution. Detect destination conflicts
and broken link ownership before archive construction. Debug output groups and
versioned SONAME/symbol policies must preserve installed ABI, not just build a
runnable binary. Generated configuration/pkg-config/man/catalogue files belong
in this graph as much as ELF files do.

Evaluate rules_pkg mappings/archives for shared conventions. Use a bounded BSD
adapter where pkgbase metadata, hardlinks or filesystem flags require it; the
standard rules_pkg docs list tar/zip/deb/rpm, not a ready-made pkgbase replacement.
The final pkgbase archive action consumes declared manifests and a declared pkg
execution tool. `component-packages.py` currently queries Make package version and
invokes package Makefiles: retain it only as an independent migration reference.
Version and ABI inputs must become explicit Bazel release inputs.

Base/hardware builds remain separate. Ports continue using Make through the
maintained hardware targets and PORTSDIR=/usr/obj/5BSD-ports; this external boundary
must record source, compiler/kernel identity and package provenance. Import only
verified hardware outputs into release composition. Preserve the single combined
repository /usr/obj/usr/src/repo: base-only results advance latest-built; only a
complete verified publication advances latest. Network publication, activation
and private-key signing are explicit controlled operations, not cached build
side effects. Do not expose signing secrets through action inputs or remote caches.
Building does not authorize installation or reboot. BIP stays out of scope.

### Execution, tests and observability

- Rules propagate transitive providers/runfiles without deep merge loops. Tools
  must carry their runtime closure, and runners must use supported runfiles lookup
  including repository mapping rather than guessing physical workspace paths.
- FreeBSD process-wrapper execution is not filesystem isolation. Prove the chosen
  sandbox denies undeclared file/network access and detects writes outside outputs;
  qualify host/runtime constraints separately. Do not promise remote execution
  until a compatible worker and complete execution-tool closure pass real builds.
- Use bazel test for unit, generator and runtime tests, plus analysis tests for
  configurations/providers/action edges and expected failures. Integration tests
  inspect cquery/aquery, BEP and execution logs. Preserve skip/expected-failure
  counts, and run privileged/VM suites separately with explicit environments.
- Qualify clean builds; warm no-op builds; changes to a source, private/public
  header, generated input, tool and option; restoration; cache reuse across clean
  roots; and isolated unrelated targets. Remote-cache correctness requires a
  separate cross-worker check; local warm success does not establish it.
- Measure analysis and action time, CPU, peak RSS, disk usage, I/O and cache bytes.
  Compare equivalent Make and Bazel products/configurations on the same machine,
  with cold and warm caches disclosed. No performance acceptance from one sample.

### Review and retirement sequence

1. Finish the shared architecture audit: configurations, SDK/bootstrap, ordinary
   C/C++ API selection, generator toolchains, runfiles, install/pkgbase and kernel.
   Classify each existing helper as retained, adapted, migration-only or removed.
2. Complete one maintained product slice end to end, including its existing tests,
   shared/static ABI, debug/install metadata and actual pkgbase archives. The first
   bzip2 BUILD files currently establish compilation only; they do not satisfy it.
3. Stabilize the public macros/providers and normal persistent frontend workflow;
   qualify multiple platforms and invalid configuration diagnostics before broad
   conversion. Preserve Make comparisons outside the required Bazel build path.
4. Convert all base libraries/programs/services, generators and kernel/module
   products. Reconcile supported product inventories against independent source
   and package inventories; every omission needs an explicit supported policy.
5. Qualify native bootstrap, full world/kernel/packages, installed boot/runtime,
   capability daemons, hardware integration, combined publication, release media
   and upgrades. Compare performance and cache/resource behavior at system scale.
6. In a disposable source copy remove base Makefiles and migration exporters, then
   rebuild/test/package from documented bootstrap inputs. Prove the Make-free base
   path through both direct Bazel and Foundry. Only then consider the default switch.

Per-component acceptance records must name the platform/configuration and graph
labels; explain any custom rule; report build/test/install/package status
separately; link retained evidence; list remaining exceptions. A converted source
list or successful fixture is not a fully converted component.

### Existing implementation disposition

**Staging cache correctness blocker (2026-10-25):** bsd_stage.bzl's directory
artifact loses hardlink identity after a confirmed disk-cache restoration into a
fresh output base. Earlier successful local staging does not qualify cache-safe
package construction. See the cache-roundtrip evidence below. The final native
package action must consume declared file/link metadata and preserve it in a
serialized package/archive; a cached directory's inode identity is not authoritative.
Do not resolve this by disabling caching or by treating separate copies as links.


| Implementation | Decision for the final architecture | Work still required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root MODULE/lock and component BUILD files | Retain and expand as authoritative definitions. | Pin/qualify bootstrap dependencies; complete component semantics and tests. |
| source_graph.py / native-qualify.py format 5 | Adapt as the normal frontend path. | Persistent build state, clean environment policy, source/action/output provenance, test inventory and runtime reporting; current input bindings do not cover the entire source closure. |
| component-plan.py, component_plans.py, component-build.py, configured_* exporters | Migration/reference only. | Retire from required builds as definitions move; preserve independent comparison evidence. |
| native_cc_toolchain_config.bzl | Retain toolchain approach, adapt implementation. | Native relocation passes; explicit configuration modes, cross platforms and complete execution closure remain. |
| native_cc.bzl / bsd_program.bzl | Review and reduce custom compile/archive machinery. | Prefer rules_cc; retain only proven object/variant requirements not represented by standard rules. |
| bsd_link_group.bzl / bsd_link_sequence.bzl | Conditional BSD link adapters. | Restrict to real GROUP/order requirements and preserve native/negative/cache evidence. |
| bsd_fidl.bzl / bsd_dtrace.bzl and other generators | Retain declared-action/provider design. | Toolchain selection, target/exec boundaries, negative analysis tests, full consumer closure. |
| bsd_kyua.bzl / bsd_compare_test.bzl | Adapt test protocol integration. | Supported runfiles lookup and transitive tool runfiles, execution runtime isolation, complete original test inventory. |
| bsd_artifacts.bzl / bsd_install.bzl / bsd_stage.bzl | Retain semantics, review standard alternatives. | Make-independent metadata ownership, tool runfiles, complete BSD artifact/parity tests. |
| component-packages.py | Independent Make comparison only. | Native pkgbase action consuming Bazel installation/package providers replaces its production role. |
| libmd_graph.bzl / cc_toolchain_config.bzl / parallel version-map implementations | Pilot duplication to reconcile. | Map remaining consumers before removal; consolidate on qualified shared rules, not multiple divergent backends. |

No deletion is implied until replacement coverage is verified. This table is a
migration disposition from the inspected shared paths, not certification of every
rule body. In particular, the source-graph runner and new BUILD files must undergo
the same acceptance review as older work. No frontend interface changed during
this architecture-only update; its required follow-up changes are listed above.

## Required end state: Bazel owns base build definitions (2026-10-25)

The maintained source of truth for the base build must be checked-in Bazel
BUILD files and reusable Starlark rules. Make metadata extraction and generated
BUILD packages are migration scaffolding, not the completed architecture.
Current component plans still depend on configured Make environments and their
include closures (`component_plans.py`); successful native compile actions do
not establish independence from Make.

Move source lists, library relationships, generated-file dependencies, per-source
options, platform selections, tests, installation metadata and package membership
into reviewed Bazel definitions. Use toolchains and platform constraints for
compiler/execution/target selection, providers for dependency information, and
explicit generator actions for generated files. Runtime installation policy is
still data: declare its files as inputs rather than encoding policy in rules.
External source and tool versions must be explicit and reproducible.

Migration order and acceptance gates:

1. Review the existing rules and emitter in bulk against the official Bazel rule,
   C++ toolchain, runfiles and sandbox documentation. Record defects, necessary
   BSD adaptations and unqualified assumptions separately.
2. Establish checked-in component definitions and shared rules with a small
   representative library/program/generator/test/package slice. Do not maintain
   a second handwritten JSON build language or retain a mandatory Make-to-Bazel
   translation step.
3. Port existing components in batches. For each batch review dependency edges,
   execution versus target tools, providers, runfiles, source flags, installation
   and package ownership. Compare with Make as an independent migration oracle.
4. Qualify each slice with native builds/tests, clean and incremental/cache
   behavior, changed-input invalidation, sandbox checks and relevant package
   parity. Measure resource/performance costs; do not infer hermeticity from a
   successful process-wrapper sandbox run.
5. Prove the normal frontend builds migrated components without invoking Make
   metadata queries or consuming prior exported plans. Prepared SDK inputs remain
   a separately disclosed bootstrap dependency until native bootstrap is proven.
6. Retire the corresponding exporter/emitter path after parity and independence
   gates pass. Keep Make for ports; any temporary base compatibility targets must
   delegate to Bazel rather than regenerate its build definitions.

Every conversion requires this review, including previously reported conversions.
The maintained build-bsd frontend, backend targets, tests and manual must follow
this transition together. No frontend behavior changes in this planning update.
Full world/kernel/package coverage and bootstrap remain unfinished.

Reference contracts:
- https://bazel.build/extending/rules
- https://bazel.build/extending/toolchains
- https://bazel.build/docs/sandboxing
- https://bazel.build/basics/hermeticity

## Native-rule architecture review: initial findings (2026-10-25)

This is a source review of the shared integration, not certification of all
25 Starlark files or all converted components. The required bulk review remains
open until every rule family and its consumers have evidence.

| Area | Observed implementation | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build ownership | `component-build.py:emit` loads configured plans; `component_plans.py` binds Make environment and include closure. | Blocking final migration: replace with maintained BUILD/Starlark definitions, not another metadata translator. |
| C/C++ compilation | `bsd_program.bzl` and `native_cc.bzl` use `cc_common`, selected C++ toolchains and `CcInfo` dependency contexts. | Retain native APIs; review custom per-source and object-order behavior against ordinary `rules_cc` before carrying it into final component definitions. |
| Archive policy | `native_cc.bzl` registers a custom archive action and accepts only exact `-crsD` / `rcsD` command shapes. | Explicit current limitation, not a general toolchain contract. Evaluate standard linking APIs and qualify member order/variants before removing or generalizing it. |
| Link sequence/GROUP | Explicit ordered archive paths and linker GROUP script preserve BSD semantics, with declared artifacts and C++ linking contexts. | Keep only where those semantics are required; do not route ordinary dependencies through special rules. |
| Runfiles aggregation | Kyua, GROUP and sequence rules merged dependencies in loops. | Changed to `merge_all`, as required by Bazel guidance to avoid deep depsets. Native regression qualification recorded separately. |
| FIDL / DTrace | Declared outputs, providers and executable tools in execution configuration; FIDL uses Args and DTrace copies objects before a mutating generator. | Useful foundations. Cross-target tool selection and full generated dependency closure still require review and execution evidence. |
| Toolchain layout | `native_cc_toolchain_config.bzl` assumes workspace-relative `toolchain/sysroot`. | Relocatability gap for a reusable external toolchain repository; resolve paths through declared toolchain artifacts in the final repository integration. |
| Test execution | `bsd_kyua.bzl` constructs directory-runfiles paths and uses host `/bin/sh`, `/usr/bin/env`; runtime checks use host loader tools. | Not hermetic or remotely qualified. Adopt supported runfiles resolution and explicit execution-platform/runtime requirements; do not claim sandbox success proves absence of host dependencies. |
| Install/debug | Declared stage and debug artifacts/providers exist, but stage policy comes from exported Make metadata. | Move ownership to maintained Bazel package definitions; preserve independent Make comparison during migration. Audit executable tool runfiles propagation as well as explicit runtime filegroups. |

Official contracts consulted: [rules](https://bazel.build/extending/rules),
[toolchains](https://bazel.build/extending/toolchains),
[runfiles merge_all](https://bazel.build/rules/lib/builtins/runfiles#merge_all),
[sandboxing](https://bazel.build/docs/sandboxing).

Priority is build-definition ownership and reusable toolchain integration before
further broad conversion through the temporary emitter. Existing mechanism
qualification remains useful but must not be counted as completed migration.
Frontend review: runfiles aggregation changes are consumed by the existing
`build-bsd bazel-test` backend; no input, CLI or manual contract changes. The
future checked-in graph entry point must be integrated there in the same change.

## Current implementation and next expansion (2026-10-25)

The maintained `build-bsd bazel-test --bazel-inputs FILE` path emits native Bazel
compile, generator, archive, link, debug, test and selected install actions.
It still reuses an explicitly selected Make-built SDK. Component success is not
world, kernel, full package, bootstrap or installed-system qualification.

Recorded evidence includes libmd test/install parity, the bzip2 package family,
additional C/C++ libraries, and 47 maintained math-test programs with 463 passing
cases. These are historical completed runs described below, not a claim that
all components were rerun against the most recent helper changes.
Native libc/libsys/compiler_rt/libc_nonshared now build together; static and
dynamic libc smoke consumers pass, with native libc/libsys loader identities
verified. Selected libc-family native staging parity now passes; the full libc
test suite, complete package families and installed-system parity remain open. No kernel or complete world build has passed through this backend.

**Completed string-suite qualification:** all 42 maintained libc string ATF programs
passed, with 138 passing cases and no skips/expected failures. The selected graph
includes libc/libsys/compiler_rt/libc_nonshared and Make-declared
ATF-C/libnetbsd/libmd dependencies. Generic libmd generation and eight shared C
test-body dependencies were fixed before this pass; earlier failures are retained.
Evidence: `/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-libc-string-native-r3-20261025/receipt.json` and
its bound `atf-results-receipt.json`. Native runtime identities and complete case
inventories were verified. The maintained frontend's compact-log option passed;
the retained execution log is 2,596,214 bytes. This is build/test qualification,
not installation, package or full-system qualification.

**Latest combined run:** string, stdbit and stdio built together through the
maintained frontend: 86 programs, 399 cases, with 396 passed, two expected failures
and one root-required skip. The source tests explicitly declare those expected
failures and privilege requirement. The receipt preserves `all_cases_passed=false`.
Evidence: `/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-libc-config-plans-r3-20261025/native/receipt.json`.
The earlier string/stdbit run had all 208 cases pass. Privileged isolated execution
and investigation of expected failures remain separate qualification work.

**Selected installation qualification:** independent re-verification of the
native libc/libsys/compiler_rt/libc_nonshared stage passed at
`bazel-libc-family-stage-r3-20261025/stage-reverification/receipt.json`: 1,902
payloads, 42 directories, 1,153 hardlinks and three symlinks. This includes
configuration/catalogue byte checks against Make and actual inode relationships.
Earlier failures are retained. Complete package families and upgrades remain open.

**Latest program compilation qualification:** native per-source C/C++ program
objects now consume effective Make contexts, preserving ordinary/PIE flags and
object order. `bazel-bzip2-program-contexts-20261025/native/receipt.json` records
both bzip2 utilities and libbz2 built through maintained build-bsd, with all six
sample tests passing. The mixed-language primitive passed source-flag isolation,
constructor retention, object-order and precise cache invalidation checks at
`bazel-program-objects-maintained-20261025`. This is not C++ base-program or
full-world qualification. Program plain-library sequences now preserve repeated
arguments; native link/runtime/invalidation fixtures pass. The first stdlib build
stopped on a missing libthr object-source declaration. That declaration and
shared-library search-path validation are fixed. The fresh `.OBJDIR`-bearing run
at `bazel-libc-stdlib-refresh-r4-20261025` built its selected targets, but only 31
of 34 ATF programs passed: two lack shared-module fixtures and one exposed the
clean runner's missing PWD. The generic PWD fix subsequently passed all eight

workspace, ignores user/system Bazel rc files, uses batch mode, and records
commands, tool/source/output hashes, and the reported version. Supply a fresh
output directory. Build products belong under `/usr/obj`, for example:

```
python3.12 tools/build/bazel/native-probe.py --src /usr/src \
  --output /usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-native-probe --bazel /usr/local/bin/bazel
```

The default parallelism is all logical CPUs. This probe intentionally uses
host headers/libraries. It does not establish hermeticity, source-tree sysroot
correctness, reproducibility, cross compilation, Make parity, or publication
readiness. Its passing result never enables a system backend.

## Base availability and Make coexistence

Bazel is required in the default installed base system, including images and
USB installations. It must be supplied by the maintained package construction
and verified combined repository, with its runtime closure, licenses and update
ownership recorded in the system manifest. Building the executable in a ports
checkout or finding a host installation does not satisfy base availability.
The package integration must account for the JDK runtime and shell dependencies;
a standalone copied Bazel launcher is insufficient. Determine the supported
Bazel/JDK versions together from the maintained custom port, then qualify them.
Do not misclassify Bazel as hardware merely to reuse the hardware package list.

Make stays installed and supported. Qualification must include conventional
world/kernel builds, package publication and representative unchanged ports
that use Make, alongside Bazel builds. Third-party build systems are not rewritten
as a condition of installation. Test upgrades and rollback of Bazel plus its
runtime packages, both tools in installed images, and no accidental dependency
on the builder's home configuration. Base provisioning is pending; this probe
does not install or package Bazel.

## Licensing and default installation

Bazel's Apache-2.0 license does not describe its complete distribution. The
selected Bazel9 port requires OpenJDK21, Bash and Python at runtime. OpenJDK
uses GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception where designated; Bash is GPLv3+;
Python uses the PSF license. Building BSD software with these tools does not
by itself change that software's license. Shipping the tools still requires
satisfying their own redistribution obligations, including applicable source
and notice requirements. A default installation containing this closure is not
an entirely permissively licensed installation.

The selected OpenJDK21 port also declares X11, font, audio and image-library
dependencies. For example, alsa-lib declares LGPL21+. The complete recursive
package closure and Bazel's bundled third-party components have not yet received
a license audit. Do not infer approval from the top-level LICENSE variable or
label unknown licenses permissive. Before default-image publication, inventory
licenses and license combinations from the actual selected packages, preserve
notices, and establish corresponding-source delivery for applicable components.
Record this beside the package hashes and update ownership. Build-only tools
must be distinguished from shipped runtime packages.

Keep Bazel and its runtime dependencies as separately identified packages in
the default system composition. Investigate a maintained headless Java variant
for footprint reduction; the current port does not supply that qualification.
No dependency may be silently excluded from the image to satisfy a size or
licensing claim. This requirement does not enable Bazel as a system backend.

License references:
- https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/LICENSE
- https://openjdk.org/legal/gplv2+ce.html

The 2026-10-24 review used the selected local ports Makefiles, not an assertion
that every transitive or bundled component had been audited.

`declared-probe.py` and `cc_toolchain_config.bzl` exercise actual Bazel C/C++
compile/link actions with a copied source-built compiler and SDK. They do not
invoke Make for compilation. Required inputs are explicit:

```
python3.12 -B tools/build/bazel/declared-probe.py --src /usr/src \
  --sysroot /usr/obj/usr/src/amd64.amd64/tmp \
  --objdump /usr/obj/usr/src/amd64.amd64/usr.bin/clang/llvm-objdump/llvm-objdump \
  --bazel /usr/local/bin/bazel --target x86_64-unknown-freebsd16.0 \
  --cpu k8 --clang-version 21 \
  --readelf /usr/bin/readelf \
  --make-library /usr/obj/usr/src/amd64.amd64/tools/build/bazel/shared-reference/libbsd_samples.so.1 \
  --output /usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-declared-pilot
```

First build the independent Make reference described below. Use a fresh output path. The CPU name is Bazel's explicit toolchain key, while
the target triple determines Clang's ABI. No cross-build qualification is implied.
Development-header symlinks are materialized into declared files. Library links
must resolve within the staged SDK. Compiler/header and linker/library filegroups
are separate, avoiding library inputs on every compile. Whole-SDK staging is a
pilot convenience and its disk/time cost is not a production performance result.

The pilot builds the real base echo source and a C++ vector/iostream test, then
injects errors into the copied source and SDK header. Each change must cause a
real failed rebuild bearing the injected diagnostic; restoring it must rebuild
successfully. It records tool/source origins, staged input hashes, commands,
output hashes and explicit qualification limits. No dependency-check suppression
or host-header fallback is used. Only the C++ target requests C++ runtime libraries.

The `bsd_static_binary` macro rejects shared requests; the separate
`bsd_shared_library` macro now exercises explicit PIC and shared-link actions.
This experimental configuration remains private to the pilot. The earlier trial
with empty/disabled shared action configurations caused a Bazel5 internal error
and was removed. The new shared metadata gate below uses real configured actions,
not that failure as evidence of compatibility.

The processwrapper sandbox does not establish full hermeticity. Bazel/Java,
embedded tools, the host kernel, and any executable runtime dependencies remain
host inputs. SDK hashing does not authenticate source provenance. The current
qualification uses installed Bazel5.4.1; Bazel9/Bzlmod, full base targets, complete dynamic
runtime/ABI coverage, cross builds, package manifests, output parity and performance remain
unqualified. Build-bsd continues selecting Make.

`runtime_test.c` is a separately Make-built static ATF helper for matching-system

## PIC and shared-object metadata gate

The toolchain now propagates the explicit target triple, staged sysroot and staged
LLD path to every executable and shared-library link action. `fully_static_link`
is enabled by static binary targets, rather than forcing `-static` onto shared
links. PIC compile actions receive `-fPIC` and BSD assembly's `-DPIC`. The shared
macro requires an explicit SONAME and enables fatal shared-textrel warnings;
links use immediate binding and RELRO to match the maintained Make defaults.

The independent reference uses `shared-reference/Makefile`, unmodified libc
strnlen.c and amd64 div.S, and the normal `bsd.lib.mk` implementation:

```
env MAKEOBJDIRPREFIX=/usr/obj make -C /usr/src buildenv \
  'BUILDENV_SHELL=make -C /usr/src/tools/build/bazel/shared-reference -j16 all'
```

The declared probe builds its own same-source shared object through Bazel, then
`elf-shared-check.py` compares ELF class/data/OS ABI/machine, SONAME and NEEDED
against the explicitly selected Make artifact. Both must have RELRO and NOW,
nonexecutable stacks, no writable-executable LOAD segment, no TEXTREL, and no
RPATH/RUNPATH. The checker records the readelf tool hash, both artifact hashes,
raw inspection output and metadata. It does not execute either library.

```
python3.12 -B tools/build/bazel/elf-shared-check-test.py \
  --readelf /usr/bin/readelf \
  --reference /usr/obj/usr/src/amd64.amd64/tools/build/bazel/shared-reference/libbsd_samples.so.1
```

Seven negative/positive metadata test cases pass. The qualified fixture has
SONAME `libbsd_samples.so.1` and NEEDED `libc.so.7`, matching Make. Evidence lives
under `/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-shared-qualified-20261024-r2/`. Its existing result
field `shared_target_rejected` refers specifically to rejection of a shared
request through the static macro, not rejection of the supported shared macro.
The source/header/assembly invalidation checks cover both archive and shared
outputs. PIC archives legitimately contain `.pic.o` members; membership checks
still require exactly the two selected real sources.

This gate does not establish exported-symbol version policy, complete ABI parity,
installed library locations, loader search/runfiles deployment, dynamic runtime
behavior, or all Make compiler policy flags. Make uses `-fpic` in this amd64
reference while the Bazel pilot uses `-fPIC`; both are PIC here, but no cross-arch
flag equivalence is assumed. Source/SDK and hardening changes can alter the static
outputs too; previous VM receipts apply only to their recorded hashes.

## Shared-library runtime fixture

`shared_runtime.c` is compiled as a dynamic PIE by the declared Bazel toolchain.
It takes one absolute library pathname, uses `dlopen(RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL)`,
resolves div/strnlen with `dlsym`, then checks each pointer with `dladdr` and
canonical file paths. Both symbol providers must be the explicitly requested
library before signed division and bounded-string tests run. Finding same-named
functions in libc cannot satisfy that check. Success requires `dlclose` too.

The static ATF launcher provides three cases with explicit configurable inputs:

- `shared_bazel`: `shared_program` loads `bazel_library`.
- `shared_make`: the same program loads the independent `make_library`.
- `shared_missing_library`: confirms `missing_library` does not exist, then
  requires the actual dlopen-failure exit status, empty stdout, and a diagnostic
  identifying that requested pathname. A loader/exec failure is a different
  status and cannot pass this control.

Default guest paths are `/usr/tests/bazel/shared_runtime`,
`/usr/tests/bazel/libbsd_samples.so.1`,
`/usr/tests/bazel/libbsd_samples-make.so.1`, and
`/usr/tests/bazel/intentionally-missing.so`. The parent runner supplies those
fixtures. The dynamic program requests `/libexec/ld-elf.so.1` and libc.so.7;
matching rtld, libc and its dependency closure must be staged from the qualified
system. Do not run against older host runtime libraries and call that system
qualification.

Compilation, dependency-invalidation and shared-metadata evidence is under
`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-shared-runtime-qualified-20261024/`. Parent-controlled VM

### Real libsbuf runtime fixture

`sbuf_runtime.c` is a declared dynamic executable with no direct libsbuf link.
It takes an absolute library pathname and resolves each tested API with
`dlvsym(..., "FBSD_1.2")`; `dladdr` and canonical path equality must identify
the requested library for every function. It checks:

- Automatic growth from a two-byte request to 4096 payload bytes, formatted
  suffix, exact length/content, finish/error/done state and clear/reuse.
- A fixed eight-byte buffer's overflow, ENOMEM propagation through finish,
  and recovery using clear.
- Partial drain callbacks consuming at most three bytes, with exact collected
  contents after finish, plus explicit EIO from a failing drain callback.

ATF cases `sbuf_bazel` and `sbuf_make` use the same program and assertions.
Inputs are `sbuf_program`, `bazel_sbuf_library` and `make_sbuf_library`, defaulting
respectively to `/usr/tests/bazel/sbuf_runtime`, `/usr/tests/bazel/libsbuf.so.6`
and `/usr/tests/bazel/libsbuf-make.so.6`. These are fixture paths, not production
library installation decisions. Existing static/shared cases remain intact.
Stage the declared output and independent Make library plus the rebuilt static
`runtime_test` in the parent's matching-system VM fixture, using the existing
rtld/libc dependency closure. This new executable has only libc as DT_NEEDED;
it loads the requested libsbuf explicitly at runtime. Compilation alone does
not count as execution evidence; the parent must bind its VM receipt to hashes.
These cases do not exhaust sbuf's API, later symbol-version sets, allocation
failure handling or concurrency behavior.

Pinned distribution repository cache
------------------------------------
repository-cache.py --archive /absolute/bazel-dist.zip --sha256 EXPECTED_SHA256
--output /usr/obj/NEW-DIRECTORY exports the distribution's content-addressed
repository cache. Supply a previously verified distribution digest. The helper
checks every cache entry against its SHA256 filename, rejects unexpected or
duplicate entries and links, and publishes NEW-DIRECTORY/cache only after all
checks pass. It never executes archive contents or merges existing caches.
Failed exports retain a FAIL receipt and cache.pending for inspection.

Use the returned directory as Bazel's --repository_cache input. This is a
cache seed, not proof that an arbitrary consumer's module graph can resolve
offline. A consumer still needs explicit module versions, a lockfile, required
registry metadata and extension inputs, followed by an actual offline build.
The current Bazel5 pilot is not converted or qualified for Bazel9 by this helper.
Native corruption/escape/duplicate checks: python3.12 -B repository-cache-test.py.

Bootstrap failure propagation
-----------------------------
bootstrap-status-test.py --buildenv /absolute/patched/scripts/bootstrap/buildenv.sh
--bash /absolute/path/to/bash checks the actual upstream run helper, extracting
its body from the supplied source. It verifies success and exit statuses 1, 37,
and 134 in verbose and quiet modes. This guards against swallowing compiler
failures through the status of shell negation. A passing test proves helper
error propagation only; it does not qualify Java execution or a Bazel build.
Run this against the source after applying the selected ports patches.

### DTrace and FIDL generation requirements — 2026-10-25

Both generators are required for the native world graph. They must not be
bypassed with stale generated files, disabled features or opaque Make actions.
The next generation work covers:

1. DTrace provider headers, declared tool/runtime inputs, selected SDK drti.o,
   and regular/PIC/PIE provider objects as requested by Make. dtrace -G rewrites
   its input objects: the Bazel action must receive copies and declare both the
   rewritten objects and provider object as outputs. Multiple providers, static
   anchors, failure propagation and incremental behavior require qualification.
2. FIDL host compiler/bootstrap dependencies, selected Python runtime, ordered
   schemas/imports, generator modules/templates, platform availability and
   per-binding flags. Native actions must declare the generated C++ sources and
   C/C++ headers and compile against declared runtime headers. Schema, template,
   compiler, flag and runtime-header changes require invalidation tests; normal
   and cross builds must distinguish host tools from target libraries.
3. Zlib pkg-config generation through the shared declared-template contract,
   followed by broader library/program migration and installation/package gates.

before removing .d inputs from SRCS. Component plans record those source hashes,

binding and uses that same list in its Make dependencies. The component exporter
records ordered FIDL schemas, library/version/flags,  generator/template hashes,
and configured generated source/header lists. Native component emission rejects
these components explicitly until their generation/C++ actions are implemented.

### Make and Bazel integration acceptance criteria

Make entry points must preserve configured build options, generated inputs,
installation metadata and pkgbase/hardware publication semantics while native
Bazel targets own compilation, generation, linking and tests. Whole-build Make
commands inside Bazel actions do not qualify as migration. Ports retain Make.

Qualification must cover explicit execution/target toolchains, typed generator
providers, transitive CcInfo, sandbox input closure, deterministic outputs,
no-op builds, selective invalidation and clean-versus-incremental equivalence.
Cache reuse across workspace locations and concurrent builds must be measured;
host tools and libraries still used implicitly must be removed or explicitly
reported before hermeticity or remote-execution support is claimed. Production
backend selection remains gated on world, kernel, install, package and runtime
parity, including DTrace and FIDL, plus disk I/O and memory measurements.

### Configured library aliases and final link order (2026-10-25)

The component planner now exports each LIBADD entry's LIB*SRCDIR, LDADD_* and
DPADD_* values from Make. The native component emitter resolves dependency labels
through these source identities using library_dependencies.py. It no longer
assumes that logical LIBADD names equal a library's output name. In particular,
pthread maps to lib/libthr (target thr), and cplusplus maps to lib/libc++
(target c++); no hand-maintained alias table is used.

The first real-config check exposed Make's intentional final reordering of
pthread/c/sys in bsd.libnames.mk. The resolver now uses final LDADD order rather
than LIBADD order. For libfidl the resulting direct targets are channel, c++,
thr. Eight maintained library-dependencies-test.py checks pass, including
reordering, aliases, missing/ambiguous components, extra linker options, groups
and repeated libraries. Repetitions/groups are rejected until typed linker

### Installed linker-script sysroot consumption check (2026-10-25)

LLD's ScriptParser::addFile rebases absolute script inputs only when the script
is inside the selected sysroot. Passing an installed script as an arbitrary
outside-sysroot linker input would therefore be unsafe: it can resolve absolute
paths against the build host. Full native graph integration must preserve the
selected sysroot or represent the script's dependency semantics explicitly.

`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-cxx-script-consumer-20261025/receipt.json` records a direct
staged-compiler test using an installed script byte-identical to the native
Bazel-generated artifact. The link trace resolves libc++.so.1 and libcxxrt.so
inside the private staged SDK. A C++ exception/string consumer runs successfully
with that SDK's library paths. A deliberately missing runtime path in the private
script fails with LLD's selected-sysroot diagnostic; restoration rebuilds and runs
successfully. Original script bytes and mode were restored. The selected target
is checked against the recorded SDK receipt.

This is not bazel test or qualification of Bazel-built libc++: it uses existing
Make-built SDK libraries and the host ELF loader. No host installation occurred.

policy-export session 51718 remains active; batched-export adoption is still

### Make/Bazel integration contract and compile-context audit (2026-10-25)

The migration target is a native Bazel action graph for base. During migration,
maintained Make metadata is the configuration authority and Make builds supply
independent parity references. Compilation, linking, code generation and tests
in the native graph must be Bazel actions with declared inputs and outputs.
Whole-component Make invocations do not qualify as native conversion. Ports
retain their own Make builds. Production frontend selection remains bsd-make
until the complete world/kernel/package/runtime gates pass.

Required integration properties, not claims of completed qualification:

- Use C++ toolchain APIs and CcInfo for compilation/linking dependencies;
  explicit providers carry generated FIDL/DTrace artifacts and installation data.
- Separate execution tools from target outputs through toolchains and platform
  constraints. Cross compilation must not execute target-built generators.
- Declare generator schemas, templates, modules, tools and runtime files. Preserve
  ordered linker inputs, source-specific flags and archive variant membership.
- Keep build-bsd and maintained world/kernel/package entry points connected to
  the qualified backend. Preserve pkgbase ownership, debug files, hardware
  identity checks and combined repository publication requirements.
- Validate incremental rebuilds with changed and unrelated inputs, clean-build
  parity and missing-dependency failures. Verify cache reuse across clean output
  roots before claiming portable cache correctness. Host dynamic-loader/runtime
  dependencies still limit current hermeticity claims.
- Qualify FreeBSD sandbox enforcement and cache behavior independently. Report
  execution strategy, cache hits, action counts, CPU, memory, disk I/O and disk
  usage. Enable workers/remote execution only after correctness and measured
  benefit; their availability alone is not a reason to use them.
- Register maintained tests with Bazel and retain machine-readable test/build
  evidence. Measure configuration/export overhead as well as action execution.

The libc++ audit found nine STATICOBJS runtime sources that belong only to its
regular archive, and C++ flags inherited from source-specific CFLAGS. The planner
now inventories STATICOBJS, ARADD, static compile flags and all C/C++ per-source
flag namespaces. The emitter rejects unsupported extra archive objects/static
flags; it does not silently omit them. Explicit object/source mapping and
per-variant effective-context integration remain unfinished.

compile_context.py queries Make with the short automatic-variable bindings

records effective language flags, static flags and dependency-file flags.

### Bounded parallel compiler-context export (2026-10-25)

component-plan.py now exports independent ordinary-source compiler contexts with
bounded workers. --jobs defaults to the host logical CPU count; --jobs 1 selects
serial queries. Ordered results preserve source/variant order. Repeated queries,
final metadata requery, input hashing and change detection remain enabled. The
shared BuildEnvironment query log uses a lock. Static-only contexts and other
metadata queries are still serial. This is configuration parallelism, not a
change to native compilation or production backend selection.

Same-input libc++ exports under /usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-libcxx-{serial,parallel}-
context-20261025 matched all configuration content, input hashes and all 248 query
records including multiplicity, ignoring only query order, elapsed time and
worker count. The maintained component-plan-compare.py accepts --left and --right
plan paths, reports receipt hashes and rejects all other differences.
component-plan-compare-test.py passed scheduling-equivalence and seven negative
cases covering flags, hashes, target settings, omitted repeated queries, failed
queries, diagnostics and unknown configuration fields. These checks do not
establish that the original configuration export itself is complete.

Measured internal elapsed time was 123.52 seconds serial versus 28.60 with 16
workers (4.32x in this single warm-run comparison). /usr/bin/time reports serial
99.56 user / 26.58 system seconds versus parallel 155.11 / 48.22: reduced latency
costs more CPU here. Serial/parallel block input operations were 19/261 and block
output operations 274/275. Reported peak RSS was 87140/87128 KiB, but this is NOT
aggregate concurrent process memory; no total-memory improvement is claimed.
export.stderr retains resource reports and comparison.json retains the original
comparison. This is not a cold-cache benchmark or world-scale performance result.

Frontend review: format-3 build-bsd qualification consumes the prepared plan;
configuration export's worker setting is independent of build-bsd compilation
jobs. No build-bsd.c switch or production target change is needed. The manual

provide int BSD_TEST_ENTRY(void), defaulting the macro to main for ordinary static
tests. A generated shared wrapper compiles with BSD_TEST_ENTRY=bsd_test_entry,
links through the same metadata-selected regular-archive targets used by native
shared components, and rejects unresolved symbols. A maintained consumer calls
that entry point. This mode requires static-only direct dependencies, native-c
and no test arguments; it is an explicit fixture, not a converted base component.

existing format-3 qualification path. Direct static and ordinary dynamic modes
retain their existing semantics.

The libsys Makefile declares TEXTUAL_SRCS.memcpy.c and consumes it in the specific
Make object prerequisites. The component planner exports source-owned textual

cc_common.compile actions, never as separately compiled .c sources or as a broad
C-file glob. Maintained textual-inputs-check.py streams the execution log and
verifies all 954 libsys regular/PIC actions, including absence of that input from
unrelated actions. This is explicit per-source metadata, not exporter knowledge
of bcopy.c. Other textual inclusions still need their own declarations.

Bazel's .pic.o member names versus Make's .pico names. Native archive construction
now uses declared artifact aliases only where configured member names differ;
the compiler still uses native cc_common actions. This adds internal symlink
actions and needs broader performance qualification, not an assumed zero cost.

A stronger audit caught another issue after the r4/r5 cache checks: restoring the
textual input did not restore original artifact hashes. Clang's DW_AT_comp_dir
contained transient processwrapper sandbox paths (observed with llvm-dwarfdump),
so recompilation changed DWARF bytes. The earlier cache receipts established exact
compile invalidation scope but did NOT establish reproducible byte restoration.
The toolchain now explicitly uses -fdebug-compilation-dir=. for compile actions.
Debug source paths remain workspace-relative; debugger source mapping and broader
cross-workspace reproducibility remain separate requirements.

textual-cache-test.py now requires explicit artifact arguments, changes the
textual input by prepending a comment (shifting debug line locations), proves that
selected artifact bytes actually change, restores the source, rebuilds, checks
exact output-byte restoration and verifies the precise recompiled source set.
The original source is restored in a finally block. No real source-tree file is
mutated. This qualifies local incremental behavior only, not remote caching.

DTrace/static-only composition and reproducibility gate (2026-10-25)
------------------------------------------------------------------
The native library rule now keeps STATICOBJS out of DTrace rewriting, matching
Make's separation of OBJS/SOBJS from regular-only additions. It appends the
static-only objects to the regular archive after rewriting ordinary objects,
then applies the complete configured archive order. A regular archive containing
only static sources is supported without DTrace; an instrumented variant without
ordinary objects remains an explicit error. The maintained component emitter
already passes both inventories, so this uses the normal build-bsd backend with
no new frontend option or installation policy.

The maintained dtrace-composition-test.py accepts explicit SDK, module workspace,
command log, Java home and output paths. It verifies SDK hashes and builds three
runtime consumers: regular/PIC instrumented libraries and a static-only library.
It checks exact archive order, excludes static-only objects from PIC and DTrace
rewrite arguments, checks original compiler input hashes, and verifies linked
DOF sections. Evidence:
/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-dtrace-composition-maintained-20261025/receipt.json.
These are disabled-probe rule fixtures, not active tracing or libc qualification.

The earlier dtrace-static-invalidation receipt checks no-op behavior, provider
invalidation, input preservation, syntax failure and successful restoration, but
never checked restored archive bytes. An additional byte comparison FAILED for
both DTrace archives; the noninstrumented static-only archive was identical.
Do not interpret functional recovery as reproducibility. Source investigation
found dt_link.c:hash_obj hashes realpath(object) into generated symbols, exposing
Bazel's changing sandbox absolute path in output. Original compiler objects are
unchanged; differences start with DTrace rewriting and propagate through linking.

The maintained dtrace-action-test.py now accepts repeated --restored-output paths
relative to its private workspace. It hashes those outputs after baseline and
restoration, writes restored-outputs.json, and fails before a passing receipt if
bytes differ. This is an open correctness/cache qualification gate. Fixing it
requires a declared, stable object identity in DTrace while preserving symbol
uniqueness; disabling sandboxing or ignoring binary differences is not a fix.
Mixed archive/shared linker GROUPs, libc's auxiliary filter, active tracing,
full world/kernel/pkgbase and matched performance qualification remain open.

Reproducibility failure reproduced by the maintained restored-output check:
/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-dtrace-reproducibility-20261025/restored-outputs.json.
The test exits nonzero and emits no passing receipt. Both instrumented archives

This is a generator input policy, not output postprocessing or sandbox removal.

### Staging hardlinks fail disk-cache restoration — 2026-10-25

Review before attaching maintained manifests to bsd_stage found that the existing
hardlink tests checked only freshly executed output trees. The maintained
install-hardlinks-test.py now has --cache-roundtrip: it builds an out-of-order
hardlink chain into a disk cache, then builds the same targets using a separate
output base. Both output bases and logs are retained; nothing is installed on the
host. The test requires an observed disk-cache hit and checks actual inode identity.

The reproduction at
`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-hardlink-cache-roundtrip-20261025/chain-cache-restore.json`
is **failed**: all three tested link relationships were lost. chain.log records
the successful initial build; chain-cache-restore.log records one disk-cache hit
and a successful Bazel build whose filesystem topology is wrong. The test exits
nonzero and does not write a passing overall receipt. This contradicts any inference
that earlier physical-stage success established cache-safe package construction.

The current tree representation must not be the final installation artifact.
Retain typed metadata and regular payload dependencies; implement package/archive
construction that encodes link identities and ownership/modes explicitly, with any
physical staging confined to that action or a deliberate external materialization
step. Qualify both cold execution and cache restoration/extraction, including
hardlink chains, symlinks, permissions and directory metadata. Disabling caches,
forcing local execution or repairing outputs after a reported build success are
not acceptable fixes. Bazel also documents symlinks inside tree artifacts as
unsupported: https://bazel.build/rules/lib/builtins/actions#declare_symlink .

Frontend review: format 5 currently builds source-owned manifests, not physical
stages or package archives. Keep that boundary until the replacement is qualified.
Historical component staging remains mechanism evidence, not production package
qualification. The build-bsd manual now identifies the cache-restoration gap.

### Compression control and stale-output inventory correction — 2026-10-25

//tools/build/bazel/config:package_threads is now an int_flag accepted through the
existing build-settings object. Zero keeps pkg's automatic threading default;
positive counts explicitly bound compression threads. World/kernel compilation
parallelism is unaffected. The package rule validates nonnegative counts during
analysis. Default selection has not been changed based on a single small family.

A directory scan after switching split/combined profiles exposed an old -man pkg
left beside the current outputs. Globbing the persistent output directory is not
a valid current artifact inventory. The package action now emits index.json as a
declared output, with exactly the generated package basenames and SHA-256 values.
package_index.py validates that index, rejects absent/changed/duplicate/traversing
entries, and ignores unlisted neighbors. Native package inspection, cache tests
and the private-root install helper now require it. The install helper also
rejects overlapping file ownership before installation. package-index-test.py
retains these boundaries as host-Python regression tests, not Bazel tests yet.

### 2026-10-25: compressed DWARF tests found and fixed a static-link defect

Native lines_static and lines_shared tests build ordinary and zlib-compressed
DWARF4 executable fixtures. They verify SHF_COMPRESSED independently, traverse
all compilation units, decode line tables and require the fixture's known source
file/line. The first test version incorrectly assumed the first CU was the test
source; linked startup CUs required fixing traversal. The corrected shared test
passed, but the static test failed decompression. An independently Make-built
archive reproduced the failure with the same consumer.

Cause: zlib_stub.c supplied a weak uncompress that could satisfy static archive
resolution before real zlib. Both normal Make and native Bazel target libraries
now omit it. Make retains the stub when BOOTSTRAPPING is defined for legacy host
compatibility. No forced linker symbol or special test-only compression fallback
was added. Query checks verify normal/legacy-bootstrap source selection; old-host
bootstrap execution is not qualified by those queries.

/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-libdwarf-tests-r3-20261025 records passing static and shared
native tests for both ordinary and compressed DWARF4. shared-runtime.txt verifies
native libdwarf/libelf/zlib resolution. make-static-check also passes against the
fixed independent Make archive. qualification now has 64 members, 359 defined
static and 361 defined dynamic symbols matching Make; all 11 generated files
and DT_NEEDED still match under the previously documented origin-comment rule.
Earlier 65-member parity receipts describe the old source state and are retained.

Native tests exposed an existing ABI bug in contrib/libcxxrt/typeinfo.cc:
__cxa_demangle returned string length instead of allocated capacity, and did
not reject a nonnull buffer with missing capacity. The implementation now
reports allocation size including the terminator, preserves an existing larger
capacity, and returns -3 for invalid arguments. This follows the Itanium C++
ABI section 3.4: https://itanium-cxx-abi.github.io/cxx-abi/abi.html#demangler
The source fix applies equally to Make and Bazel.

buffer reuse, capacity preservation, malformed external-name and invalid-argument
tests. shared-runtime.txt confirms the native DSO. An independently rebuilt
Make archive passes the same checks in bazel-libcxxrt-make-fixed-20261025;
that check uses host cc. Earlier failed test results remain retained.

was accepted by the underlying demangler (a leading type code can be consumed
without rejecting trailing input). The final test uses malformed external

retain that parser issue for follow-up rather than claiming full grammar
conformance. Full exceptions/unwinding/dynamic_cast, alternate ABI, installation,

cased in the writer, and no filesystem flags are set on build outputs.

correctly; unknown flags and inconsistent hardlink metadata are rejected. All

restoration of system immutable flags. The pkg_create.py guard against flagged
payloads remains: package creation/extraction needs separate qualification
before that guard can be removed. This is traditional BSD file metadata, not
revived BIP policy work.

Bazel tests. timer_static links the actual component archive; timer_shared uses

### Kernel-module completion gate (2026-10-26)

The full native kernel migration includes base kernel modules, not only the
kernel executable. Source-owned Bazel declarations must account for module
selection, selected kernel configuration, generated option/interface headers,
assembly and C inputs, and supported target architectures. Dependencies must
invalidate affected module actions when those inputs change. Completion
requires configured module inventory reconciliation against Make, installation
and debug/pkgbase metadata parity, and matching-kernel VM load/functionality
checks with unload checks for modules that support unloading. Module coverage
is not established by successful userspace component builds.

Third-party kernel modules can remain ports/Make builds. Keep the maintained
separate hardware targets, PORTSDIR selection and kernel/hardware identity
checks before verified combined publication under /usr/obj/usr/src/repo.
Neither building nor publishing authorizes host installation or reboot.
The build-bsd frontend must expose qualified kernel configuration/module
selection through maintained backend inputs when that implementation lands;
these requirements do not imply that the kernel backend is qualified today.

### Bounded Make/Bazel sort resource comparison (2026-10-26)

bazel-sort-performance-20261026 retains a replayable diagnostic harness,
seeded 500,000-record (5 MB) shuffled input, raw time -l logs, all twelve run
records and a summary receipt. The already qualified threaded executables use
the same native libmd and host libc/libthr. Three repetitions per build/workload
alternate execution order and request all sixteen logical CPUs. Each output is
checked against independently constructed ascending-record SHA256; every run
passes. Input, executable and library hashes remain unchanged. Verified output
copies are removed to avoid retaining twelve identical files; hashes remain.

With a 64 MiB buffer, median process elapsed time is 0.43 seconds for both;
median CPU seconds are 0.42 native and 0.43 Make, with peak RSS medians 69736 KiB
and 69732 KiB. Both have 39 median block-output operations. With a 256 KiB
buffer, process elapsed medians are 0.42 native and 0.43 Make; CPU medians
0.41/0.42 seconds, RSS 4716/4708 KiB, and block-output medians 211 for both.
Scratch sampling observes over 120 files and roughly 5.4 MB logical temporary
data in the small-buffer case, versus none in the large-buffer samples. All
scratch files are cleaned by sort after each successful run.

These results show no large observed regression on these two bounded workloads.
They are not performance acceptance: runs are short, the host is shared, caches
are not cold, and requested parallelism does not prove observed concurrency.
Process block-operation counts do not measure physical bytes/device latency;
ZFS compressed/allocated scratch sizes and 20 ms samples are not peak device
usage. The wrapper elapsed_seconds includes subprocess polling overhead; the
receipt's time_real_seconds comes from time -l and is the comparison used above.
Broader disk-I/O patterns, sustained workloads, native kernel/runtime and
controlled performance thresholds remain open. Frontend review: this measures
frozen qualified outputs without changing build inputs, frontend or publication
semantics. Make remains production/default.

### Native libc++ in libdevdctl/zfsd; ABI header boundary (2026-10-26)

libdevdctl and zfsd now declare native libc++/libcxxrt/libm dependencies, remove
SDK -lc++/-lm link flags and use -nostdinc++ with source-tree C++ headers. The
first compile exposed a dependency-interface defect: libcxxrt's private atomic.h
search root propagated into zfsd and shadowed OpenZFS's atomic.h inside extern C.
The fix makes libcxxrt headers implementation_deps and removes them from
libc++'s public dependency context. libc++ compilation still declares the ABI
headers privately; its private static-archive target retains necessary inputs.
No zfsd/OpenZFS source edits, include-order overrides or compatibility shims were
introduced to suppress the error.

bazel-zfsd-native-libcxx-r2-20261026 retains nineteen consumer compile actions
(five libdevdctl sources in two variants plus nine zfsd sources), all using
-nostdinc++ without private ABI/libc++ implementation search roots. Link parameter
records select native C++ shared targets without SDK fallback flags. Independent
Make installation comparisons pass all three zfsd entries and nine libdevdctl
entries, including header/manual bytes, metadata, symlink and debug linkage.
Four focused libc++/libcxxrt tests report cached passes, zero fresh executions.

No daemon was executed. These changes have build/install/dependency evidence;
event handling, reconnects, pool operations and runtime daemon integration remain
unqualified. Existing earlier CLI evidence does not prove behavior after this
change. Complete native library/package/world/kernel and performance gates also
remain open. Frontend review: existing build-bsd format-5 target/test lists and
maintained installation helpers cover this transition with sixteen build CPUs;
no CLI, security, signing or publication policy changes are needed. Make remains
default.

### chflags host failure diagnosis (2026-10-26)

The failure above is now traced to a capability-rights ABI mismatch between the
running host kernel and the source SDK libc. A read-only cap_rights_get probe on
stdout returns index-1 word 0x040000006fffffff; the SDK headers define the full
word as 0x05fc000001ffffff. The returned unknown bits are 0x000000006e000000,
and SDK libc cap_rights_is_valid returns false. The installed host header still
allocates the local jail/timer/fcntl/advice rights in low bits; current source
allocates them at high bits to avoid collisions with upstream rights.

Evidence (probe source, executable, stdout, input hashes and host identity) is
retained in bazel-chflags-install-20261026/qualification/rights-diagnosis.json
and rights-probe.*. The core backtrace reaches cap_rights_intersect from the
stdio limiting helper, before the requested flag operation. This is not a
Bazel-only compilation failure. No assertion, permission restriction or unknown
bit was removed to obtain a pass. Runtime qualification requires a matching
kernel/userland VM; old/new ABI upgrade compatibility is a separate unresolved
system concern. The existing host failure remains recorded as failed.

Frontend review: no build input or production policy change was made in this
diagnosis. Existing explicit SDK and VM qualification routes remain applicable;
no build-bsd.c changes are required. Candidate counts are unchanged.

### newfs structured image comparison (2026-10-26)

comparison. Evidence and executable/source checkers are retained under

compiled against the declared SDK derives field offsets from struct fs and backup
superblock locations from each image's cylinder-group geometry. It checks regular
file bounds, UFS2 identity, superblock sizes, geometry agreement and enabled
superblock checksums. No list of observed differing byte addresses supplies the
comparison policy.

superblock before comparing copies with only fs_time and its checksum field
cleared in memory. Original images remain unchanged. The five superblocks in
the failed pair all validate; their write times differ by exactly one second,
and every other image byte matches. The original failed byte comparison is still
retained. Four negative checks reject changes to an ordinary image byte, a
superblock field, a checksum and a timestamp without a new checksum.

under this validated timestamp policy, and -N leaves both 64 MiB regular files

accepts only this native-endian UFS2 checksum-enabled comparison scope; it is not

### Maintained frontend output snapshots (2026-10-26)

Format-5 source_graph.py now requests the default, metadata and directory_metadata
output groups and freezes their local regular-file outputs before releasing its
persistent-state lock. bep_artifacts.py consumes target-completion/configuration
identities and transitive NamedSetOfFiles records from the completed BEP stream.
It does not infer outputs from target names or shared bazel-bin paths. Files must
match Bazel's SHA-256 and length before and after copying; missing/changed files,
unsupported URIs/digests, incomplete groups, missing/cyclic file sets and unsafe
logical paths fail qualification. Aspect outputs are kept out of ordinary target
capture. This follows Bazel's documented BEP graph, including out-of-order events:
https://bazel.build/versions/7.3.0/remote/bep-examples

Snapshots live under each run's artifacts directory. Content-addressed private
blobs deduplicate shared outputs; manifest.json records target/configuration,
original logical name/URI, mode, size and digest. Receipts bind the manifest hash
and capture-helper source hash. Directories use mode 0700 and blobs 0400, avoiding
broader exposure when capturing restrictive build outputs. These are retained
evidence files, not installed or directly runnable trees. Event input is streamed;
shared file sets are visited once per target instead of recursively materializing
repeated flattened lists. This change adds output read/copy/hash I/O proportional
to captured files; it is not a zero-cost or performance-qualified operation.

Thirteen focused helper tests pass, covering transitive/out-of-order graph reads,
retention after overwrite, deduplication, metadata groups/private modes, stale or
missing files, missing/cyclic sets, unsafe paths, unsupported URIs, missing digest,
incomplete groups and aspect separation. Five existing setting tests also pass.
These are host Python checks, not native Bazel test targets.

Real 16-job frontend evidence under /usr/obj/usr/src includes
bazel-artifact-snapshot-disabled-r2-20261026 and
bazel-artifact-snapshot-enabled-r2-20261026. After switching configurations, both
captured archives still match the preceding independently Make-audited archives,
and their captured metadata has nine and fifty records respectively. Disabled
capture stores three unique files/135271 bytes; enabled capture stores four

Format-5 test-result accounting previously required returned testSummary labels
to equal the requested labels literally. This incorrectly rejected successful
test_suite requests because Bazel reports the expanded individual tests. The
frontend now queries tests(set(requested labels)) with the same SDK override,
platforms and typed build settings after the build/test command, while retaining
the frontend lock. Labels are quoted as query strings. It records configured
individual labels in test-inventory.json and binds that file's hash in the receipt.
The exact expanded set must match passing BEP summaries. Missing, extra, duplicate,
failed or skipped summaries fail qualification; nonempty requests expanding to
zero tests also fail. Direct-test and build-only behavior remain supported.

### Shared execution-log reader performance correction (2026-10-26)

execution_log.py now supplies the package cache, component archive cache and
libmd archive-variant qualification helpers. It reads concatenated JSON objects
incrementally and grows incomplete records geometrically, avoiding both whole-log
suffix copies and repeated fixed-chunk reparsing of large input lists. Memory
retains the pending record rather than the full text. Non-object, truncated and
malformed records fail instead of silently ending qualification. The libmd
verifier retains archive and compile records needed for its original checks;
source-mutation and warm-action checks remain intact.

execution-log-test.py passes four tests covering large records across read
boundaries, Unicode/escapes, empty/whitespace input, malformed/truncated tails
and non-object records. bazel-execution-log-reader-20261026/measurement.json reads
the retained 1,146,671,801-byte log with 1,251 records in 8.30 seconds and 47,472 KiB
maximum RSS, versus 62.93 seconds for the preceding fixed-chunk parser on that
log. This is a harness measurement, not a compiler or system performance claim.
libmd-regression.json rechecks the retained fastbuild/dbg/opt/force-PIC evidence,
both 28-object archives, declared inputs, compile flags, empty warm execution
and semantic source-change recompilation successfully. Five changed Python files
also parse successfully; no system builds were rerun just to test the parser.

Frontend review: this changes qualification evidence readers only. Build inputs,
