### Capsicum host/SDK ABI mismatch isolated (2026-10-26)

The runtime failure is now localized by a read-only cap_rights_get probe in
bazel-capsicum-abi-diagnosis-20261026. The same source is compiled against host
and SDK headers/libraries. Opening /dev/null and querying its rights changes no
capability restrictions. Host libc reports valid=1; SDK libc reports valid=0.
Both receive word1=040000006fffffff from the running kernel. Host CAP_ALL1 is
040000006fffffff; SDK CAP_ALL1 is 05fc000001ffffff. The returned bits excluded by
the SDK mask are exactly 000000006e000000. Word0 agrees. Compiler commands,
outputs, kernel identity and header hashes are retained in results.json.

Installed/source header comparison shows 5BSD-local jail, timerfd, read-ahead
and fadvise rights moved to high word1 bits while upstream rights occupy some
former positions. caph_limit_stream obtains current rights and passes them to
cap_rights_intersect; SDK validation rejects the old kernel's bit set before
limiting it. This explains the observed Make/native assertion without relying
only on matching crashes. It is an ABI mismatch, not merely a newer source date.

A kernel/userspace environment with matching rights definitions is needed for
qualification. Upgrade compatibility also needs explicit review: masking unknown
bits or accepting validity is not a semantic translation of reassigned rights.
No kernel, libc, rights policy, host installation or reboot was changed here.
The probe narrows the runtime gate but does not close it. Frontend inputs are
unchanged; counts remain 201/77/4 and Make remains default.

### Native ATF outcome reporting and pthread lifecycle coverage (2026-10-26)

The native adapter now distinguishes `passed`, `skipped`, and
`expected_failure`. Bazel action success is not a count of passing cases.
Using Bazel's `XML_OUTPUT_FILE` protocol, skips and expected failures produce
explicit XML skipped records with their reasons. They remain nonpassing cases.
An uninstrumented caller without XML reporting still requires an actual pass.
Crashes, nonzero exits, cleanup failures, unexpected passes reported by ATF,
malformed records, and unsupported expected exit/signal/timeout results fail.
Result text uses getline rather than a fixed reason-length limit.
Protocol reference: https://bazel.build/reference/test-encyclopedia.

The format-5 backend now retains test logs and XML from BEP test-result events
under `test-reports`, with hashes and separate recorded case counts. Counts
cover all recorded attempts, including retries; a successful action summary
cannot alone establish that all cases passed. The maintained frontend manual
explains this distinction. No new command-line switch or build-bsd.c parser
change is needed. These are reporting changes, not fixes for pthread PR 211802.

The adapter lifecycle suite has 13 passing focused tests, including expected
failure/skip reasons, long reasons, XML escaping, malformed results, crash and
cleanup failure rejection, and fail-closed non-XML callers. Three report capture
checks and eight configured test inventory checks pass. The upstream join and
detach cases are now declared native Bazel tests using native libthr and ATF;
their execution and the full frontend outcome check are recorded below.

### Maintained native SFTP ATF suite (2026-10-26)

A standalone read-only cap_rights_get/is_valid probe independently confirms the
host/source SDK mismatch without Bazel: host libc accepts rights returned by
the running kernel, while SDK libc rejects them. Word 1 is 040000006fffffff;
the SDK allowed mask is 05fc000001ffffff, leaving unsupported bits 6e000000.
The probe source, binary hashes, ldd resolutions, uname and outputs are retained
beside that package receipt as bazel-cap-rights-probe.{c,json}. caph_limit_stream
passes those kernel-returned rights to cap_rights_intersect, whose source libc
validity assertion explains the dirname/tr crashes. Matching-kernel runtime
qualification remains required. No security checks were disabled, and this is
not evidence of successful SSH authentication or live audit enforcement.

### Capsicum host/source mismatch confirmed (2026-10-27)

A read-only static probe calls cap_rights_get(1), prints the compiled CAP_ALL
mask and kernel-returned mask, then calls cap_rights_is_valid without intersection.
Compiled against the source SDK it reports all=02000fffffffffff:05fc000001ffffff,
returned=02000fffffffffff:040000006fffffff, valid=0. The same probe compiled against
host headers/libc reports all equal to returned and valid=1. Thus the current
source libc rejects rights returned by this older host kernel. caph_limit_stream
reads the current rights then intersects them; its assertion is explained by this
mismatch. No assertions or rights were changed. This evidence is stronger than
the earlier inferred mismatch, but does not qualify the shell suite on a matching
kernel or establish cross-version runtime compatibility.

Evidence: /usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-capsicum-host-abi-20261027 contains source,
static probe binaries, commands, hashes, outputs and host uname. Compiler is the
host cc with an explicit source sysroot for the source variant; this is an ABI
diagnostic, not another Bazel-built component. Matching-kernel qualification
remains necessary; no host installation, upgrade or reboot was performed.
Frontend review: no build input/policy contract changed; this is a runtime-gate
finding, so no CLI or backend implementation change is required.

The direct adapter now supports declared body_timeout_seconds and
cleanup_timeout_seconds. It blocks SIGCHLD before fork, uses monotonic deadlines
and sigtimedwait (no periodic polling), isolates each phase in a process group,
and kills remaining group members when a phase finishes. A timed-out body still
runs cleanup; timeout in either phase fails even if the body wrote "passed".
FreeBSD requires a caught SIGCHLD disposition for these timed waits; a regression
caught the initial default-disposition mistake and the corrected runner passes.

All 17 host lifecycle tests pass, including hung body, hung cleanup, descendant
pipe closure, ordinary deadline completion, invalid limits and existing result/
cleanup checks. The maintained frontend then built the runner and actually

binds the standalone regression command/results to the changed source hashes.

Cleanup defaults to Kyua's 300 seconds. The outer Bazel timeout must leave room

Process groups do not contain a deliberately detached session. Unsupported ATF

### 2026-10-27 section-scoped DTrace generation prerequisite

DTrace now has an opt-in `-x linksection=index` for `-G`. It accepts a positive
decimal ELF section index, requires exactly one relocatable input with an
executable section at that index, and processes only relocations targeting that
section. Invalid indices/options and multiple-object requests fail before input
rewriting. The default still processes all sections. The dtrace(1) manual
explains the caller's obligation to process all required sections and associate
metadata and registration code correctly; the option itself is not a GC fix.

The native tool/library rebuilt through the maintained frontend with 16 CPUs.
`dtrace-section-filter-test.py` verifies 16 generation cases using tools and
inputs checked against the captured action log: default output references both
functions, each filter references only its function, other code bytes remain
unchanged, sequential processing rewrites both sections, repeated processing
produces identical metadata, and invalid requests fail without input changes.
The test uses an ELF64 little-endian fixture parser, not a production ELF writer.
It does not establish active probe registration/firing or linker association.

/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-dtrace-section-filter-check-20261027. The latter contains
commands.json, receipt.json, retained verifier, and default-parity.json. All ten
captured outputs of the unchanged default-mode archive experiment are

### 2026-10-27 native section-associated archive prototype

The opt-in archive runner now discovers probe-bearing sections from ELF
relocations, generates a separate DOF record for each using linksection, and
associates generated registration/finalization arrays with that DOF using
SHF_LINK_ORDER. It combines code and providers with the declared linker using
`-r --unique`, preserving their section boundaries. A final relocation scan
associates each DOF with its unique code section. Original application
constructors are never reclassified. It rejects missing/multi-section parents
rather than arbitrarily selecting one. Extended symbol section indices are not
yet supported by the helper and fail explicitly. No production library selects
this experiment.

The ELF transformation uses native GElf rather than the earlier ELF64-only
experiment parser. Association scans are linear in the section/relocation
inventory; they do not rescan all relocations for each DOF. DTrace invocation
per code section and duplicated provider registration/debug data still need
real-library resource/size measurement before adoption. GElf use alone does not
establish multi-architecture qualification.

Ten native Bazel tests now inspect function, DOF and registration/finalization
symbol counts and execute their captured fixture binaries. Cases cover plain
and unselected archive members, one/two selected instrumented members, dead
callers, multiple function sections in one source, shared probe/is-enabled
symbols, and ordinary application initialization with observable side effects.
R4 executed six passing cases and four failures because clang optimized the
fixture's ordinary initializer into static data. Inspection of the original
compiler object proved the initializer was absent before rewriting. The fixture
now uses observable state and checks it at runtime. R5 executed those four
corrected cases successfully and reused the six previous passing results.
This evidence covers linker retention and executable behavior, not live probes.

### 2026-10-27 bundle registry migration and long-path correctness fix

Added native bundle_registry_test with registry/selection sources and explicit
shared capbundle/UCL/ATF dependencies. All eight maintained cases are declared;
five retain root requirements. Three unprivileged cases run. The first run
exposed an undeclared mkdir fixture command; native mkdir and libxo are now
explicit runtime inputs. The fixture's existing system() still uses the system
shell, so this is not a hermetic shell-runtime claim.

The next run exposed a genuine libcapbundle bug: open_bundle copied a full path
into its 256-byte name buffer before looking for the final slash. Deep paths
could silently produce a parent directory or truncated name. The implementation
now extracts the basename from the full path first and rejects path/name copy
truncation. The maintained per_user_agent_loads_with_owner regression explicitly
creates a parent path longer than NAME_MAX, ensuring the failure is reproducible
outside Bazel's deep test directory. No shortened test path or alternate library
was substituted. All three unprivileged registry cases pass after the fix.
The existing libcapbundle host suite also passes after rebuilding the library.

The registry binary matches recorded Make defined global symbols and ELF linkage;
the reference predates the regression extension, so this is structural comparison,
not a claim of a fresh Make runtime qualification. Evidence:
/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-switchboard-registry{,-r2,-r3}-20261027 and
/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-libcapbundle-basename-20261027. Initial missing-tool and
long-path failures are retained. Five root cases, full installation and broader
Switchboard/runtime gates remain open.

### 2026-10-27 explicit final-consumer static link sequence

Added bsd_link_sequence using CcInfo/cc_common APIs. Bazel's ordinary topological
DAG traversal does not guarantee declaration-order precedence when libraries share
dependencies (https://bazel.build/rules/lib/builtins/depset). This opt-in boundary
visits complete dependency linker-input sequences in the requested order, preserves
the first occurrence of each LinkerInput, and encodes them as a dependency chain.
It retains LibraryToLink objects, owners, flags and additional inputs unchanged;
cc_binary still creates the link action through the configured toolchain. No
archive paths, symbol names, replacement linker or shell command are embedded.
Flattening is confined to the two final Capsule consumers, not every library.

member/link-order investigation; do not normalize these differences away.

### HID field runtime regression and shared-source correction (2026-10-27)

The initial libusbhid build/install evidence did not qualify report field access.
The native `//lib/libusbhid:data_test` now places each report against a PROT_NONE
page and checks 5,120 combinations: widths 1–32, bit offsets 0–7, report ID
present/absent, signed/unsigned extraction, and five value patterns. An independent
bit model verifies writes preserve surrounding bits. This is one reported Bazel
test case containing those combinations, not 5,120 separately reported cases.

Before the fix, the test exited 139 (retained failure-test-reports in
`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-usbhid-data-before-20261027`). The old inclusive byte
endpoint touched beyond exact-size reports; its shifts also could exceed the
32-bit intermediate. The shared data.c now touches only occupied bytes, uses a
64-bit unsigned intermediate for five-byte unaligned fields, and performs unsigned
mask/sign extension. Setter width is capped at 32 consistently with getter and
value argument. API still has no buffer length: callers must supply a valid
item and enough bytes. Invalid descriptors and widths outside 1–32 are not
covered by this regression.

`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-usbhid-data-after-20261027` records an executed passing
Bazel test. `/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-usbhid-fixed-20261027` rebuilds the static/shared
library, both consumers and their install archives; its test result is cached.
The Make library was rebuilt/staged in
`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-libusbhid-data-make-20261027`, and the same test also passes
against that archive using the host compiler/runtime. Retained qualification
checks confirm 19 static and 21 shared globals, SONAME and dependencies, all 21
installation records, 13 hardlinks, 15 exact nonbinary files, and debug association.
Sources, hashes, comparisons and Make runtime record are retained under the fixed
run's qualification/libusbhid directory. Previous consumer parity receipts remain
historical; this run establishes their rebuild, not new consumer runtime checks.

Frontend review: maintained build-bsd bazel-test already accepts the format-5
native target/test inputs; no new build input, packaging or publication semantics
were introduced and no frontend C change is needed. No device operations, host
installation, USB daemon execution or live DTrace/audit qualification occurred.
This is a library runtime fix, not evidence of complete world/kernel qualification.

### libc++ extraction diagnosis from BSDLog tests (2026-10-27)

Removed unconditional alwayslink from libc++ charconv. Its original purpose was
shared export retention, but it also forced character-conversion code into static
consumers. cxx_shared now directly names both cxx and charconv as shared roots;
cc_shared_library retains direct roots without imposing that policy on ordinary
static consumers. This uses native rules_cc semantics documented at
https://bazel.build/versions/7.7.0/reference/be/c-cpp#cc_shared_library.

/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-bsdlog-cxx-link-20261027: existing shared and static libc++
runtime comparisons both pass. All 2050 shared definitions match the Make-built
libc++.so.1 at /usr/obj/usr/src/amd64.amd64/lib/libc++ (this is an existing world
baseline, not a freshly rebuilt libc++ reference). The four BSDLog executables
still link statically. Config symbols match exactly; each other test now has
339 native-only globals, reduced from 352. Exact differences remain failures.

Further diagnosis corrects the earlier blanket description of extra code:
representative remaining symbols (_ZTIa, __cxa_throw, __gxx_personality_v0) exist
as local symbols in Make but globals in native binaries. Make libc++.a embeds
ABI objects compiled with its hidden visibility policy. The current public cxx
CcInfo instead pulls the separately compiled libcxxrt dependency. Correct this
static/shared modeling across consumers; do not add symbol filters or visibility
flags to individual tests. The maintained static_archive already models embedded
ABI objects, but integrating it into consumer linkage without breaking shared
export ownership remains next work. Existing source kernel runtime failures are
unaffected and were not rerun.

Frontend review: format-5 targets/tests exercise the changed graph; no new inputs,
CLI or publication behavior are introduced. No host install or production-default
change. Evidence scripts and exact differences are under qualification.

### Service-control runtime diagnosis and full installation (2026-10-27)

The shell setup assertion is reproducible without ATF. The retained probe in
`/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-service-control-tests-r2-20261027/capsicum-diagnostic`
opens /dev/null and queries its rights. The host returns words
02000fffffffffff,040000006fffffff. Host libc accepts these; with the declared SDK
libc/libsys the identical probe reports cap_rights_is_valid false. Installed
headers have CAP_ALL1 payload 0x000000006FFFFFFF, while SDK/source headers use
0x01FC000001FFFFFF. The staged cap_rights_intersect assertion therefore rejects
rights returned by this older kernel. This establishes the host/SDK Capsicum ABI
mismatch behind the observed assertion. No mask, assertion, libc, utility or
application source was weakened; runtime qualification requires a matching
kernel. Nine shell cases remain unqualified.

Make's shell wrappers, helper binaries, Kyuafiles, package tags and debug files.

## Explicit secureboot header generation — 2026-10-27

Added bsd_secureboot_headers and secureboot_headers.py. The rule takes an
explicit format-1 policy, public certificate labels and optional self-test
certificate labels. Certificate files are ordered by source short path. It
produces ta.h, vse.h and secureboot_config.h using declared Python/runtime
inputs. No site files, signing clients, directory discovery, wall clock or
file mtimes are consulted. Epoch, hashes, signature algorithms, extensions,
compiled-only trust, public-anchor requirement, self-test mode and KAT string
are explicit policy fields. Compiled-only mode requires public anchors.
RSA/ECDSA are supported; unsupported algorithms including OpenPGP are rejected.
This is a generation interface, not yet the production library configuration.

Public-only PEM framing follows the maintained validator; certificate decoding
remains the verifier's responsibility. Signature extensions match Make's actual
sorted/deduplicated emission. C byte formatting matches file2c -sx. Self-test
hashes are derived from the declared UTF-8 KAT string. String-literal escaping
and policy validation reject code injection and unsupported values.

Evidence: /usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-secureboot-headers-r2-20261027. The native
//lib/libsecureboot/tests:headers_test compiles and runs generated headers with
an explicitly empty-trust fixture. It is not a deployable boot policy. Separately,
35 maintained host reference checks compare framing acceptance with public-trust.awk
and byte emission with the staged Make file2c, and test malformed/private inputs,
policy rejection, cross-file certificate boundaries and changed epoch/certificate
output. Invocation and input hashes are retained in qualification/reference-checks.json.
The initial missing generated include interface was corrected with a cc_library
header provider; its failed output remains in bazel-secureboot-headers-20261027.

## Native signed-file and in-process trust rotation — 2026-10-27

//lib/libsecureboot/tests:signed_rotation_test generates two disposable RSA-2048
keys in memory using native libcrypto, creates self-signed public certificates,
and signs files with SHA256/PKCS#1. It exercises production verify_signed and
trust-add/revoke APIs using native libsecureboot/BearSSL. OpenSSL configuration
loading is disabled, private keys are never written, and all public certificates,
signatures and payloads live beneath TEST_TMPDIR. Certificate time enforcement
is enabled with newly generated certificates; no host trust or enforcement state
is modified.

Evidence: /usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-secureboot-signed-r2-20261027. One Bazel test
passes 25 internal checks: untrusted rejection; old/new trust overlap; mismatched
certificate/signature rejection while both roots are trusted; old-root revocation
and denial even after re-addition; accepted and tampered files of sizes 0, 1,
4095, 4096, 4097 and 65537; revoked-certificate replacement; malformed/missing
signature; missing certificate; and successful new-key verification afterward.
The test generates fresh keys when executed, and cached execution must not be
reported as a fresh key generation. The earlier 23-check run is retained at
bazel-secureboot-signed-20261027.

build-bsd runs this through the existing format-5 target/test and explicit
trust inputs with 16 jobs; the manual documents scope and no C/backend contract
change is required. This qualifies self-signed RSA signer trust changes inside
one verifier process. It does not qualify firmware keys, signed image transitions,
persisted revocation, rollback resistance, boot-environment upgrades, intermediate
certificate chains, expiry boundary tests or the complete signing algorithm matrix.
Those system/key-management and broader migration/performance gates remain open.

## Capsicum runtime failure diagnosed (2026-10-27)

The cat ATF startup failure is reproducible with the host's old Capsicum ABI.
A small C probe opens /dev/null and obtains rights using cap_rights_get, built
once with installed headers/libraries and once with the authenticated SDK
sysroot. Both executions return rights words 02000fffffffffff and
040000006fffffff. Host CAP_ALL matches; SDK CAP_ALL is 02000fffffffffff and
05fc000001ffffff. Returned index-1 bits 0x6e000000 are outside the SDK's valid
mask, explaining cap_rights_is_valid rejecting the inherited rights before
cat's test bodies execute.

Commit fc21f4e34df moved local rights on October 8 and explicitly requires a
coordinated kernel/world upgrade. The running kernel was built October 7.
Some old rights also overlap newly allocated upstream rights, so masking
unknown bits is not a sound ABI compatibility fix. Keep the existing failed
Make/native runtime results. Qualification requires a matching kernel/world
runtime; neither changing PATH to host helpers nor suppressing the assertion
qualifies the candidate. No host installation or reboot was performed.

Probe source, both executables and results.json are retained under
/usr/obj/usr/src/bazel-cat-tests-20261027/qualification/capsicum-abi.
This evidence explains the shared startup failure; it does not establish
that the 13 cat cases pass on a matching runtime. The frontend and backend
require no implementation changes for this diagnostic-only update.

### Kyua suites with relative fixture layouts

`bsd_kyua_test(program_path = "component/test_program", ...)` stages the
program at a normalized relative path under the suite root. The adapter emits
a root Kyuafile and includes the component Kyuafile, as Kyua requires bare
program basenames within each Kyuafile. `suite_files` paths remain relative to
the suite root, so shared parent fixtures can be declared without traversal.
Paths must not be absolute or contain empty, dot or parent components. Runtime
libraries, when selected, are placed beside the nested executable. Individual
case selection and typed result reconciliation retain the full relative path.
The default remains the executable basename for existing flat suites. This
layout support does not remove the adapter's documented host-runtime limits.

The bintrans legacy suite qualifies this layout and all five original TAP
checks; lastcomm qualifies the existing flat layout. Evidence is recorded in
the 2026-10-28 checkpoint. Bintrans's two ATF cases still fail at runtime startup
on the current host and are not qualified by the passing legacy suite.


### Login feature and capability-database inputs

`//tools/build/bazel/config:setuid_login` is a boolean source setting, default
true, corresponding to MK_SETUID_LOGIN. The normal format-5 `build-settings`
object passes it through build-bsd bazel-test. Native login also honors existing
`audit` and `dtrace` settings. Setuid installation preserves Make's 4555/schg
metadata; disabled installation is 0555 without schg. These are installation
records, not changes to host executable permissions.

`bsd_capability_database` declares capability sources, `.db` output, explicit `little` or
`big` byte order and an execution-configured compiler. login uses the native
cap_mkdb_bootstrap source reader and amd64 little endian. Other execution/target
platforms need qualification; no host database is imported. login.conf.db is
intentionally generated rather than packaged: packages/utilities/utilities.ucl
contains its post-install regeneration and construction declaration. login exposes
package-backed install_manifest and separate generated_manifest; install_archive
includes both. Component package_layout consumes only the package-backed manifest. Full-feature and all-three-disabled
login artifact comparisons pass; authentication/session runtime remains open.


### libc cancellation-point unwind setting

The native libc semaphore group accepts the format-5 `build-settings` entry
`"//tools/build/bazel/config:thread_stack_unwind": true` (the default).
Set it to `false` to select libc's `NO_THREAD_STACK_UNWIND` behavior. This setting
currently applies to `//lib/libc/gen:semaphore_objects`; ordinary libc groups do
not receive `-fexceptions`. It does not yet select librt/libthr unwind variants.
Use the existing `//tools/build/bazel/config:dtrace` boolean independently.
The semaphore archives contain raw objects pending complete libc DOF/linking;
compiling these targets does not establish runtime cancellation or tracing.

### Effective feature selectors (2026-10-28)

Native bool flags represent requested options. Shared `*_enabled` config_settings
also require implemented prerequisites, matching Make's effective option rules.
For example `openssh_enabled` requires openssh, openssl and crypt; disabling
OpenSSL therefore excludes its dependent rc services without manually clearing
each child flag. The crypt/OpenSSL-disabled rc variants match independent Make
installation references. Remaining option relationships and compiled-world
variants are still being qualified; this is not complete src.opts.mk coverage.

The shared selectors also require MAIL for Sendmail, NETGRAPH for Bluetooth,
and OFED for OFED_EXTRA. `mail` and `netgraph` are default-on native bool flags;
`ofed` already exists. Set these through format-5 `build-settings`, for example
`"//tools/build/bazel/config:netgraph": false`. An explicitly enabled child cannot
override its disabled prerequisite. These selectors currently qualify rc service
installation; complete world inclusion and other MAIL children remain pending.
